items.title: The migration checklist for cross-border growth

items.content_html:
Expanding into a new market rarely fails on media budget — it fails on the translation of intent. These are the five principles we use to make campaigns travel.

  • Localise the offer, not just the copy - Translation is table stakes. What actually moves the needle is adapting the promotion, pricing and proof to what the local buyer already trusts.
  • Rebuild the funnel per market - Awareness in one country is consideration in another. Map where demand already exists before deciding how much to spend creating it.
  • Respect the channel mix - The dominant platform shifts by region. Lead with the channel your audience actually lives on, not the one that worked back home.
  • Measure in one currency of truth - Normalise every market to the same metric — contribution margin, not last-click ROAS — so you can compare and reallocate without bias.
  • Staff for the timezone - Speed of iteration wins launches. Put decision-making close to the market so tests don't wait 12 hours for approval.

items.title: Creative testing without burning budget

items.content_html:
Most creative budgets are spent proving what we already suspected. A lean testing framework finds winners faster — and for less.

Start with a hypothesis, not an asset

Every test should answer a question ("does social proof beat urgency?"), so even a loser teaches you something reusable.

Test one variable at a time

Hook, format, or offer — change one, hold the rest. Bundled changes give you a result you can't explain or repeat.

Small, controlled, honest

Equal budget, same audience, enough time to reach significance. Cheap tests that can't conclude are the most expensive kind.

Kill fast, scale slower

Cut clear losers early, but let winners prove themselves before you pour spend in — early winners regress more often than you'd like.

items.title: Attribution you can actually act on

items.content_html:
Perfect attribution doesn't exist. Useful attribution does — the kind that tells you what to do on Monday morning.

Pick one model and commit

The value isn't in the model's accuracy, it's in applying the same lens consistently so trends are comparable over time.

Fix the tracking foundation

Server-side tracking and clean event naming beat any clever model sitting on top of messy data.

Validate with incrementality

Geo-tests and holdouts answer the only question that matters: what would have happened anyway?

Tie every metric to a decision

If a dashboard number wouldn't change a budget or a bid, stop reporting it. Measurement exists to drive action.
